rationale: The admitted v2 makes a structural rather than rhetorical change: it abandons the proposed quasi-exclusive building concession and does not claim proprietary charging software or data. The new mechanism uses a non-exclusive property-manager portfolio relationship to screen buildings, requires at least three refundable resident deposits and a qualified report confirming usable headroom, and permits deployment only after building approval, counsel-reviewed asset-hosting terms, and executed third-party finance. A ring-fenced vehicle would then hold the financed shared asset while the operator earns origination and recurring asset-servicing fees. This changes the economics by removing founder-funded hardware and hardware markup, capping pre-deployment validation capital, and making demand, legal rights, electrical feasibility, and finance explicit go/no-go gates. The redesign does not assume that any manager agreement, asset-hosting right, resident deposits, or financing facility already exists; their obtainability remains unresolved and must be validated before deployment. Incumbent copying, OCPP switching, regulated delivery dependencies, uncertain willingness to pay, and the absence of a proven data moat remain material risks, but they no longer contradict a thesis based on statutory exclusivity or proprietary technology.
